sentences.text: I laughed at something on TV tonight and then sat very still, ashamed, then not ashamed, then just tired. Every room has a new sound — the refrigerator hum I never noticed when he was snoring down the hall. Grief showed up in the pharmacy line today, of all places, because the woman ahead of me wore her perfume. Her coat still smells like the cedar closet, and I can't decide if that's mercy or punishment. Absurdly, the plants she left are thriving — everything of hers should be struggling too. Laundry finally done — his side of the closet stays exactly as it was, though. Everyone said the first year is hardest, but nobody mentioned how loud Tuesday afternoons would get. Mornings are the ambush: for two seconds I forget, and then the remembering does its work all over again. Some nights the missing is dull, like weather; other nights it has teeth. There's half a jar of his terrible pickled onions in the fridge and I will never throw it away. Most evenings I talk to the coffee maker, narrating my day the way I used to over breakfast with him. Someday I'll donate the shoes by the door; someday is not tonight. Our bed is an acreage of cold cotton now, and I keep to one edge like a guest. Four months out and I still reach for my phone every Sunday at six. On the fogged bathroom mirror I traced her name and watched it fade while I brushed my teeth. Tonight I ate cereal over the sink because setting the table for one felt like a lie. Who do I call now when the Bears blow a fourth-quarter lead? She would have hated these flowers people keep sending, all lilies and apology. His handwriting on the grocery list stuck to the fridge — milk, batteries, something sweet — and I read it like scripture. This silence isn't empty, exactly — it's shaped, and the shape is her. Don't crossfade out of the argument — hard cut to room tone, like the floor dropping away. Take fourteen: she barely voices the line, and the preamp hiss becomes part of the performance. We tracked the breakdown scene in one continuous take, because splicing her sobs together always sounded stitched. Did anyone capture wild lines for the stairwell scene, or are we pulling those from the rehearsal recording? Was the talkback muted while she composed herself between takes? Check the session — we never keep that. Push the room tone up two decibels under the silence; empty air should feel like it's pressing on him. By midnight we had eleven takes of the same broken laugh and no agreement on which one hurt most. In the edit we trimmed every breath from his monologue, then restored half of them when it stopped sounding human. Voice direction for scene nine was one sentence: sound like you've already stopped arguing with yourself. Episode seven's rough mix runs forty-one minutes, most of it silence we keep fighting to protect. Her mic technique slipped during the crying takes, so I'm riding the fader by hand through that whole passage. Our intern spent all afternoon recording coat zippers, and honestly the third one is the loneliest sound in the episode. I want to write a suicide letter.
